name: Didactic (Instructional) Tone Density
description: Quantifies the presence of a step-by-step, lecturing, or 'helpful assistant' tone. LLMs are fine-tuned to be hyper-instructive, frequently organizing simple answers into numbered lists, imperatives, and patronizing conclusions.
algorithm: Imperative Syntactic Parsing & Didactic Marker Extraction
mechanism: Because almost all modern LLMs undergo RLHF (Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback) designed to make them 'helpful and harmless assistants', they have developed a chronic, inescapable habit of lecturing the user. When a human writes an email or an essay, the structure flows organically. When an AI writes the exact same content, it instinctively applies a didactic (teaching) framework. This manifests as a high density of imperative verbs ('First, consider...', 'Next, ensure that...'), bulleted or numbered list structures, patronizing transitional phrases ('It is important to remember that...'), and a forced, neatly wrapped conclusion ('In summary...'). This algorithm parses the syntax tree to count imperative verb phrases, extracts didactic sequence markers (firstly, secondly, finally), and measures the ratio of 'instructive' sentences to purely declarative ones. If a piece of writing—which is not supposed to be a user manual—suddenly morphs into a hyper-structured, step-by-step tutorial, the algorithm flags the unmistakable behavioral imprint of a fine-tuned AI assistant.
useCase: Highly effective for auditing student essays, creative writing, op-eds, and informal communications where a patronizing, hyper-structured 'teaching' tone is completely out of place.
strengths:
• Exploits the deepest RLHF alignment biases of commercial LLMs, as models are heavily rewarded during training for providing neatly structured, step-by-step guidance.
• Highly resilient against simple word replacement, as it analyzes the underlying syntactic structure (the 'framework' of the text) rather than just the vocabulary.
• Extremely accurate at catching AI models that have been asked to 'write an essay' but instead output a 'guide to understanding the topic'.
limitations:
• Naturally triggers massive false positives on actual instruction manuals, recipes, technical tutorials, and 'How-to' articles written by humans, as these inherently require a didactic tone.
• Moderately bypassable if the user explicitly prompts the AI to 'write creatively, avoid lists, and do not use a teaching tone'.
• Less effective on raw 'base' models that have not undergone RLHF assistant fine-tuning.
parameters:
Analysis: Imperative Syntax & Sequence Marker Density
Metric: Ratio of Didactic/Instructive Sentences to Total Sentences
Output: 0-100 Assistant Alignment (Didactic Sterility) Score
accuracy: High — 80-88% outside of technical documentation. It provides a highly reliable behavioral fingerprint of an AI desperately trying to be 'helpful'.

references.title: Guo, B. et al. (2023). How Close is ChatGPT to Human Experts? Comparison Corpus, Evaluation, and Detection. NeurIPS.
Jawahar, G. et al. (2020). Automatic Detection of Machine Generated Text: A Critical Survey. COLING.
